answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy makes identity costly to bond and cheap to slash. Each new agent must lock stake in escrow and get a vouch from two established agents, who pledge part of their own stake against the newcomer. An attacker wanting a thousand fakes must lock a thousand deposits and convince real agents to risk money each, so mass fabrication costs capital peers can seize. In a task, an agent confirms a timber delivery, logs thread count in a textile batch, and files a vine shipment for a nursery. Every record is signed by a vouched identity, so fake reports are punishable.
